subject.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode ghost connections after gateway restart silently drop inbound messages

question: Should Slack Socket Mode stay warning-only when Slack reports multiple active connections, or should OpenClaw add an automatic recovery/fencing policy for suspected same-gateway restart ghosts?
rationale: Slack/OpenClaw docs allow multiple active Socket Mode connections when routing is equivalent, while this report describes silent message loss from stale restart ghosts; automation cannot choose the false-positive and compatibility tradeoff safely.

options.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
options.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then add Slack-plugin recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts while preserving relay, HTTP, and equivalent multi-gateway setups.

options.title: Keep warning-only
options.body: Treat the current diagnostic and deployment docs as policy, accepting operator wait-and-restart recovery until stronger evidence justifies intervention.

options.title: Push production scale to relay or HTTP
options.body: Document direct Socket Mode as single-gateway operationally and route higher-reliability or multi-gateway users to relay mode or HTTP Request URLs.

recommendation.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
recommendation.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then add Slack-plugin recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts while preserving relay, HTTP, and equivalent multi-gateway setups.
